description.narrative:
Sida stödjer DKT i Myanmar i syfte att öka kunskap om och tillgång till sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter samt bidra till förändringar i attityder och beteenden, framförallt hos unga. Sidas stöd bidrar också till att höja kunskapen i Myanmar kring frågor som rör sexuell, reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter.
DKT marknadsför och säljer preventivmedel i Myanmar och arbetar på ett innovativt sätt för att stärka kompetens hos såväl konsumenter som hos de som tillhandahåller dessa produkter. DKT arbetar med social marknadsföring och kampanjer för att bidra till en mer positiv och rättighetsbaserad hållning i förhållande till sexualitet bland unga människor och ungdomsledare.
DKT använder sig av tre strategiska ingångar:
1) Ökad kunskap och val kring SRHR frågor 2) Ökad tillgång och användande av olika preventivmedel 3) Ökad kvalitet, service och information kring SRHR produkte

Sida’s support to DKT in Myanmar aims to increase knowledge about and access to sexual and reproductive health and rights as well as to contribute to changes in attitudes and behaviour, in particular among young people. Sida’s support also contributes to raising awareness in Myanmar about issues related to sexual and reproductive health and rights.
DKT markets and sells a complete range of high-quality contraceptives and safe-maternity products and builds the capacity of both consumers and providers alike to use such products. DKT works with social marketing and campaigns to foster more open and positive and rights-based attitudes toward sexuality among young people and young leaders. A normalization of the topic in homes, on streets and in the medical establishment will have a transformative effect on behaviors, with women and men empowered to make informed choices, rather than being steered by stigmas and fear. The key strategies of the program are to:
1) Increase knowledge of SRHR knowledge and choice; 2) Increasing availability and use of SRHR products; and 3) Raise quality of SRHR goods, services and information.

The intended outcomes of the program are the following:
- Increased knowledge of SRHR and choice - Increased availability and use of SRHR products - Raised quality of SRHR goods, services and information.

Between 2018 and 2024, DKT Myanmar transitioned from a startup into a resilient, self-financing, and high-impact provider of sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. Operating amid political instability, a global pandemic, and widespread displacement, the programme sustained nationwide access to modern contraception, introduced integrated service delivery, and promoted behavioral change. Key Achievements Adaptability and Continuity: DKT successfully shifted from in-person outreach and training to digital platforms, decentralized delivery models, and private-sector partnerships, ensuring uninterrupted SRHR services during severe disruptions in public-sector systems. Financial Sustainability: Donor cost per couple year of protection (CYP) declined from USD 4.84 in 2017 to USD 1.32 in 2024, while total sales revenue grew from USD 745,069 to USD 4,512,237. By 2024, DKT covered 107% of operational costs through sales revenue, compared to 40% in 2017. Service Reach and Impact: Over the programme period, DKT imported more than USD 11.5 million in SRHR commodities, reached 223 townships, and delivered approximately 5.8 million CYPs. Health impact indicators improved significantly, with pregnancies averted rising from 92,036 in 2017 to 231,527 in 2024, and unsafe abortions averted increasing from 33,088 to 99,178. Programme Objectives and Outcomes SRHR Education and Youth Engagement: Initially implemented through peer-led education in universities and industrial zones, the programme trained 123 youth counselors. Following COVID-19 and political restrictions, activities shifted to digital platforms and social media campaigns, maintaining SRHR information dissemination despite reduced scale. Access to SRHR Information: Digital platforms such as thiloyarmay.org and social media campaigns expanded reach, with contraceptive product pages attracting 1.9 million followers and condom-related pages reaching 1.1 million. Campaigns like Lets Fiesta engaged up to 6.5 million users. Healthcare Provider Capacity Building: DKT trained 7,282 healthcare providers (92% from the private sector), including specialized training on contraceptive technology. Around 300 private clinics were strengthened to deliver SRHR services, ensuring service continuity amid public-sector collapse. Availability and Use of SRHR Products: The programme distributed over 52 million condoms, and achieved a 20-fold increase in implant uptake during early years. Despite later challenges such as import restrictions, DKT maintained national-level commodity importation and decentralized distribution capacity. Overall Impact DKT Myanmar demonstrated strong adaptability, efficiency, and resilience in sustaining SRHR services under crisis conditions. While some indicators declined toward the end of the period due to external shocks, overall results reflect meaningful contributions to SRHR access and health outcomes. Continued flexibility, monitoring, and support will be critical to reaching vulnerable populations in the future.
